root_cause.text: The AppArmor profile removal logic utilized recursive function calls to traverse and free nested profile structures, causing kernel stack exhaustion when processing deeply nested profiles.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "The profile removal code uses recursion when removing nested profiles, which can lead to kernel stack exhaustion," and the patch replaces the recursive `__aa_profile_list_release()` call within `__remove_profile()` with an iterative loop implementation in `security/apparmor/policy.c`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix profile removal to properly clean up each child profile's resources instead of relying on bulk release that may leak labels and directories
intent_record.what: Replaced __aa_profile_list_release() call with explicit loop iterating through child profiles, adding curr/to_remove variables and calling aa_label_remove(), __aafs_profile_rmdir(), and __list_remove_profile() for each child profile
intent_record.how: Ensures each child profile is individually cleaned up (label removed, directory removed, list entry removed) before parent removal, preventing resource leaks that occurred when using bulk release without per-profile cleanup
